steps.title: A map to test on
steps.body: The Training yard is a sample map with room to place things, a checkpoint flag and a save point by its entrance. You add your own flag and save point to it in this course. One undo takes the whole yard away again.
steps.task: Open the World menu and click “Add the Training yard”.

how.text: Open the menu “World” in the bar at the very top and click “Add the Training yard”. The new map opens in the 3D view: a fenced yard with dummies, a wall, a knight, a hill — and a checkpoint flag and a save point by the entrance.

steps.title: How the game saves
steps.body: A save keeps the player's progress: where the hero is, what they carry, the game's variables, and everything that changed on the maps they visited (opened chests, smashed walls, beaten enemies). Saves are player data: they are kept in the browser, never in the project. The Project tab's Saving section decides how players save.
steps.task: In Project › Saving: Save anywhere, 2 save slots, Autosave on.

how.text: At the top of the panel on the right, click the tab “Project”. The game's settings open: Game, Saving, Limits and Files.

do.say: Click the tab “Project” at the top of the right panel.

how.text: In the section “Saving”, open the list “How players save” and pick “Save anywhere (Pause › Save game)”. Players can then save from the pause menu at any time; save points and checkpoints still work too.

do.say: Pick “Save anywhere (Pause › Save game)” in “How players save”.

how.text: Open the list “Save slots” just below and pick 2. Pause › Save game will then offer Slot 1 and Slot 2, so a player can keep two games.

Make sure the box “Autosave” is ticked (click it if it is empty). With Autosave on, the game saves by itself in its own Autosave slot when the hero touches a checkpoint or goes through a gate to another map.

steps.title: A checkpoint
steps.body: A Checkpoint flag is an asset marked Checkpoint (Asset studio › Checkpoint). In Play, when the hero touches it, the flag goes up: from then on Retry (after game over) and falling off the world bring the hero back there, and the game autosaves.
steps.task: Place a Checkpoint flag on the map.

how.text: In the dock at the bottom, open the tab “Assets” and click the card “Checkpoint flag” (a white pole with a red flag at its foot). The Place tool (B) turns on with the flag in hand.

do.say: Click the card “Checkpoint flag” in the Assets dock.

how.text: Click the ground in the 3D view, somewhere inside the yard the hero walks past (for example near the hill): the flag is placed there. The yard's own flag by the entrance stays; the newest one touched is the checkpoint.

do.say: Click the ground near the start to place it.

steps.title: A save point
steps.body: A Save point is an asset whose interaction is Save: in Play, “E · Save” shows when the hero is next to it, and E saves the game to the slot in use. In “Only at save points” mode, this is the only way players can save.
steps.task: Place a Save point on the map.

how.text: In the Assets dock, click the card “Save point” (a blue pillar with a light-blue top).

do.say: Click the card “Save point” in the Assets dock.

how.text: Click the ground near your flag to place it.

do.say: Click the ground to place the save point.

steps.title: Save while playing
steps.body: In Play: walk into the Checkpoint flag — the flag goes up and “Checkpoint · saved” shows at the bottom. Walk to the Save point and press E: “Game saved · Slot 1”. Press Esc for the pause menu: “Save game” opens the slots (Slot 1, Slot 2) — click one to save there; “Load game” opens the same list to load one back; “Restart from checkpoint” puts you back at the flag.
steps.task: Play the yard (Play › Play this map), touch a flag, then save at a save point (E).

how.text: Open the menu “Play” at the top and click “Play this map”: the Training yard runs in the 3D view, from its entrance.
Walk (WASD) into a Checkpoint flag: it goes up and “Checkpoint · saved” shows at the bottom. Then walk to a Save point and press E: “Game saved · Slot 1”. (Or press Esc and pick Save game › Slot 1.)

steps.title: Continue
steps.body: Stop throws the play away, as a player closing the game. Ctrl F5 plays from the first screen, like the exported game: the title screen now shows “Continue” above “Play”. Continue loads the newest save (the autosave or a slot) — here the Training yard, with the flag up — while Play starts a new game from the beginning.
steps.task: Stop, then play from the first screen (Ctrl F5) and see Continue on the title.

how.text: Press Stop in the bar at the top (or Esc twice, then Stop).

Open the Play menu and click “Play from the first screen (splash, title)” (Ctrl F5). After the splash, the title shows Continue and Play. Click Continue: you are back where you saved, with the flag up.

steps.title: A fresh start
steps.body: Saves you make while testing stay in this browser until you delete them. Project › Saving lists them; “Delete these saves” removes them, so the next test starts from the beginning and the title hides Continue.
steps.task: Stop, then delete the test saves in Project › Saving.

how.text: Press Stop in the bar at the top.
On the right, tab “Project”, section “Saving”: under “Saves made while testing” you see your saves (Slot 1, Autosave). Click “Delete these saves”.

steps.title: Your game saves
steps.body: Players can now quit and come back. Logic can save too: the cards Save game, Load game and Set checkpoint (category Saving). Saves keep working after you change the game: things a save mentions that you have since deleted are skipped.
